transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just can't seem to shut my brain off anymore. It's like... it starts with one small concern, like a client not responding to an email or something. But within minutes, my mind just runs with it, and I'm completely convinced I'm going to lose the contract, which means I'll fall behind on my divorce payments, and then I start thinking I'll never get back to a real leadership role. It just spirals, and I can't stop it.
How long have you been dealing with this kind of uncontrollable worrying?

It's been going on for a little over a year now. I lost my job, I was fired, about thirteen months ago, and that's when it really started. I managed to pick up some contract work since then, but the worrying... it just never really let up.
Besides work and finances, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life, like your health, family, or everyday minor matters?

Yeah, it really just bleeds into everything. My mind keeps jumping around from the contract work to how I'm going to make the mortgage payments... and then I start agonizing over my reputation. I worry constantly about whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm damaged goods after getting let go. Even minor things set it off. Like, if a recruiter just delays an email by a day, it suddenly feels like absolute proof that my whole career is closing down. So it's not just the immediate bills, it's... it's just everything connected to my life and future constantly cycling in my head.
Have you noticed any physical tension in your body, like tight or aching muscles, when you are worrying like this?

Yeah, definitely. I feel wound up almost all day long. It's like my shoulders are just permanently locked, you know? Like I'm constantly braced for bad news. I'll find myself pacing around the house or bouncing my leg when I'm on calls, even if nothing stressful is actually happening in that moment. I just can't seem to physically relax.
How has all of this worrying been affecting your sleep?

It's really taking a toll. Most nights I just lie there replaying interview answers in my head, or I find myself checking the clock at 2 or 3 a.m. And... well, even on the nights when I actually manage to get what should be enough sleep, I don't feel rested at all. I wake up feeling like I spent the whole night on call for a major system outage. It's just exhausting.
